articles.title: India's Tricolour in Boston Harbour: The Three-Masted Barque That Sailed Into America's Birthday Party
articles.excerpt: INS Sudarshini, a 513-ton sail training ship on a ten-month transoceanic odyssey, docked at Boston Fish Pier for the Sail250 celebrations — and the public can walk aboard through July 15.
articles.image_caption: INS Sudarshini flying the Indian tricolour during the Sail250 Parade of Sails off the Virginia coast
articles.nri_angle: India's naval sailing vessel is docked in Boston through July 15, giving NRIs in New England a rare chance to walk the decks of an active Indian warship — a floating embassy of maritime heritage at America's 250th birthday.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Florida Man Killed After Fleeing US Immigration Agents, 3rd Death in a Week
articles.excerpt: Tragic incident highlights ongoing tensions surrounding US immigration enforcement.
articles.image_caption: ICE agents in action or a protest against immigration enforcement
articles.nri_angle: The incident highlights the urgent need for reform in U.S. immigration policies impacting Indian families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thirty-Seven Defendants, Three Gangs, One Assassination: Inside the US Indictment That Finally Named Nijjar's Killers
articles.excerpt: Operation Hardball charges Lawrence Bishnoi with directing the 2023 murder of a Sikh leader from an Indian prison cell. India says it will cooperate. The diaspora is still counting the cost.
articles.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the federal prosecutors who unsealed the Bishnoi indictment
articles.nri_angle: The Bishnoi gang systematically used high-profile killings to terrorize the Indian diaspora in North America, targeting religious, social, and political leaders. The indictment is the most significant legal action yet addressing transnational criminal threats to Sikh and Indian communities abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Grocery Store Burned Before It Opened. A Mosque Replica Set Ablaze on a Bonfire. Inside Northern Ireland's Summer of Hate.
articles.excerpt: Belfast's June riots left 27 people homeless and an Indian community shaken. A month later, the arsonists have moved on to bonfires — and the 10,000 Indians in Northern Ireland are still waiting for the institutions to catch up.
articles.image_caption: Belfast, Northern Ireland — where anti-immigrant riots in June 2026 shattered the Indian community's sense of safety (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Northern Ireland's Indian community — roughly 10,000 people, many of them doctors, shopkeepers, and IT professionals who chose Belfast for its affordability — found itself at the centre of anti-immigrant riots in June 2026. The violence, including the arson of an Indian grocery store, exposed the growing vulnerability of diaspora communities in the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eleven Thousand Years of India, One Museum in Washington: The Diaspora's Audacious Bid to Tell Its Own Story
articles.excerpt: An Atlanta-based educationist has spent eight years building a case for a $14 million heritage centre in the American capital. He has now asked the Indian Embassy for a building it bought thirteen years ago.
articles.image_caption: The Embassy of India in Washington, D.C., where organisers have proposed housing the heritage museum
articles.nri_angle: A first-of-its-kind museum aimed at helping younger Indian Americans connect with their civilisational heritage, built by and for the diaspora
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Hundred and Fifty Dancers, Seventeen Countries, Three Nights Under the Acropolis: Inside the World Festival of Indian Dance
articles.excerpt: The fourth edition of the UNESCO-endorsed classical Indian dance festival opens in Athens this week, with performers from the United States, Canada, Britain, Oman, South Africa, and a dozen other nations gathering at the foot of Western civilisation's most famous monument.
articles.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer performing at the Khajuraho Dance Festival earlier in 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indian classical dance traditions carried and performed by diaspora communities across 17 countries, showcasing how NRIs preserve and project cultural heritage on a global stage
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian-Origin Leaders Tapped to Co-Lead Federal Reserve Policy Task Forces
articles.excerpt: Raghuram Rajan, Raj Chetty, and Xbox CEO Sarah Bond (born Asha Sharma) will co-chair three of the Fed's five review panels — an unprecedented concentration of diaspora talent at the heart of U.S. monetary policy.
articles.image_caption: Raghuram Rajan, former RBI Governor and IMF Chief Economist, will co-chair the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet Policy review
articles.nri_angle: Three Indian-origin figures simultaneously co-leading Federal Reserve policy review panels — spanning economics, data science, and corporate leadership — signals the breadth of diaspora influence in U.S. economic policymaking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India-UK Trade Deal Goes Live on July 15 — What Changes for NRIs in Britain
articles.excerpt: The new trade pact eliminates dual social security contributions for Indian workers in the UK, saves them roughly 25 per cent of salary, and opens 1,800 annual mobility slots for chefs, yoga instructors, and classical musicians.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds at the signing of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
articles.nri_angle: 75,000+ Indian professionals in Britain stand to save roughly 25 per cent of salary through the social security pact, while new mobility pathways and tariff reductions reshape the economic relationship between the diaspora's two largest host countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Congressman Ro Khanna Detained at Gunpoint by Israeli Settlers in West Bank
articles.excerpt: The Silicon Valley lawmaker — a potential 2028 presidential candidate and grandson of an Indian freedom fighter — says IDF soldiers sided with the armed settlers who held his group for 75 minutes.
articles.image_caption: Congressman Ro Khanna, who represents California's 17th congressional district in Silicon Valley
articles.nri_angle: Khanna is among the most prominent Indian Americans in U.S. politics, a potential 2028 presidential candidate whose family story — from a freedom fighter's household in Punjab to Silicon Valley — embodies the trajectory of the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shrey Parikh Wins Scripps Spelling Bee With Record-Setting Performance — 31 of Last 37 Champions Are Indian American
articles.excerpt: The fourteen-year-old from California spelled 32 words in 90 seconds, breaking the spell-off record and extending the Indian American community's remarkable quarter-century dominance of the competition.
articles.image_caption: The stage at the Scripps National Spelling Bee, where Indian American contestants have dominated for a quarter century
articles.nri_angle: Indian American children have won 31 of the last 37 Scripps National Spelling Bees, a dynasty fuelled by community networks, immigrant-family educational investment, and organisations like the North South Foundation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Fremont to Parsippany: Indian-Origin Mayors Are Making History Across America
articles.excerpt: Raj Salwan and Pulkit Desai lead a growing wave of Indian Americans winning local elections, reflecting the community's deepening civic roots.
articles.image_caption: Raj Salwan, the first Indian American mayor of Fremont, California
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans are translating decades of private-sector success into local political leadership, with first-generation immigrants winning mayoral races in diverse cities from California to New Jersey.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Neurologist Wins Lifetime Achievement Award for Transforming Global Stroke Care
articles.excerpt: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, founder of Mission Thrombectomy active in over ninety countries, honoured for reshaping how the world treats the leading cause of disability.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, based at the University of Miami, received a Lifetime Achievement Award for transforming global stroke care
articles.nri_angle: Yavagal's career traces the circuit of the Indian medical diaspora — training in India, research breakthroughs at American institutions, and a global initiative that channels those advances back to underserved communities worldwide, including in South Asia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ninety Artists, Eleven Days, One Ruptured World: Inside Vancouver's Indian Summer Festival
articles.excerpt: The sixteenth edition of Canada's premier South Asian arts festival is using comedy, raga, plant bioelectricity, and a closing ceremony in the Punjabi Market to argue that gathering is resistance.
articles.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer performs at an Indian dance festival
articles.nri_angle: The festival is one of North America's largest platforms for South Asian artistic expression in the diaspora — a space where second-generation identity, cross-cultural collaboration, and community building happen through art rather than politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Billionaire, the Doctor, and the Toss-Up: Vivek Ramaswamy's Ohio Governor Race Just Got Real
articles.excerpt: Cook Political Report shifts the Ohio race from 'Lean Republican' to a dead heat. Polls show Ramaswamy and Democrat Amy Acton locked at 47-47 in a state Trump won by eight points.
articles.image_caption: Vivek Ramaswamy at a campaign event
articles.nri_angle: Ramaswamy's candidacy represents a new threshold for Indian American political ambition — a first-generation Indian American competing at parity in a major swing-state governor race, while the community's relationship with his brand of politics remains deeply divided.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Months of America's Remittance Tax: The One Per Cent Levy That Rewired How the Diaspora Sends Money Home
articles.excerpt: What began as a five per cent scare in Congress ended up as a one per cent excise tax on certain transfers. Half a year into enforcement, the real effects are subtler — and more uneven — than either side predicted.
articles.image_caption: The United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., where the One Big Beautiful Bill Act was passed
articles.nri_angle: Every H-1B holder, green card carrier, and naturalised citizen who sends money to family in India now operates under this law. The exemptions favour those who bank digitally; the tax bites hardest on cash-and-counter senders — a distinction that splits the diaspora along class lines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to Seven Per Cent on Dollar Deposits. The Window Closes in Eleven Weeks.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's special swap facility has removed the hedging cost that kept FCNR(B) rates stuck below four per cent. Indian Bank alone is targeting two billion dollars by September. Here is what NRIs need to know before the deadline.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, which launched the special forex swap window for NRI deposits
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs parking idle dollars in US savings accounts yielding under one per cent, or even in Treasuries at four-and-a-half per cent, this is a rare moment when parking money in India carries no currency risk and pays meaningfully more — but only until September 30.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tax Department Can Now See Your Foreign Bank Accounts. Here Is What Every NRI Needs to Know.
articles.excerpt: A CBDT order integrates overseas financial data from over a hundred countries into taxpayers' Annual Information Statements, closing one of the last gaps in cross-border tax visibility.
articles.image_caption: Aaykar Bhavan, the Income Tax Department's office in Pune, India
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with bank accounts, investments, or property in India now face unprecedented transparency — their overseas financial information from the US, UK, Canada, and other AEOI countries will appear in their Indian tax records, raising the compliance stakes for the 30-million-strong diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Indian Sailor Missing, Ten Rescued After Iran Strikes Container Ship in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt: The attack on the GFS Galaxy is the fourth time in three months that a vessel with Indian crew has been hit in the Hormuz standoff. India's 300,000-strong seafaring community is running out of safe passage.
articles.image_caption: Naval vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, where Indian-crewed commercial ships have repeatedly been struck since April 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers — over 300,000 strong — are disproportionately exposed to the Hormuz standoff. Four ships with Indian crews have been struck since April. Maritime families in coastal India and across the diaspora live with a unique anxiety each time a vessel is hit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Tandoor to Michelin: Indian Fine Dining Is Conquering the World's Most Demanding Markets
articles.excerpt: A wave of Indian-origin restaurateurs and chefs — from the Sethi siblings in London to new outposts in Las Vegas, New York, and Dubai — is rewriting the global fine-dining map.
articles.image_caption: Indian fine dining has moved beyond the neighbourhood curry house, with restaurants like Gymkhana accumulating Michelin stars across London, Dubai, and beyond
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin chefs and restaurateurs are leading the global expansion, reshaping perceptions of Indian cuisine and building cultural bridges through food.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sunil Bharti Mittal Calls Indian Diaspora a 'Beautiful Bridge' as USISPF Honours Him with Leadership Award
articles.excerpt: The Bharti Enterprises founder was honoured alongside RTX's Christopher Calio and Fairfax Financial's V. Prem Watsa at the IX USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington.
articles.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal at the USISPF Leadership Summit
articles.nri_angle: Mittal's speech directly celebrated the five-million-strong Indian diaspora in the US as the connective tissue between the two nations, with trade deal implications for NRI business leaders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Thousand Visas, Working Holidays, and a Twenty-Billion-Dollar Promise. Inside the India–New Zealand FTA's Diaspora Dividend.
articles.excerpt: The landmark free-trade agreement signed in April and celebrated during Modi's Wellington visit this week contains the most NRI-friendly mobility provisions India has ever secured from a developed nation. A breakdown of what it means for professionals, students, and young Indians.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. The two nations signed a landmark Free Trade Agreement in April 2026. (Photo: Government of India via Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: This FTA is the most NRI-friendly mobility framework India has secured from a developed nation. The 5,000 skilled-worker visa quota, uncapped student admissions with extended post-study work rights, and 1,000 working-holiday visas create a structured pathway for Indians to live, work, and study in New Zealand — directly benefiting the 350,000-strong Indian Kiwi community and millions of prospective migrants.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The American India Foundation Just Raised a Record $3.8 Million in One Night. Here Is Why It Matters.
articles.excerpt: At its twenty-fifth-anniversary gala inside Cipriani Wall Street, AIF honoured Infosys CEO Salil Parekh, retired TD Bank chief Bharat Masrani, and BNY — while setting a new fundraising benchmark for Indian diaspora philanthropy in the United States.
articles.image_caption: The American India Foundation raised a record .8 million at its 25th-anniversary gala in New York
articles.nri_angle: The AIF gala is one of the single largest diaspora fundraising events on the US calendar. Its record haul underscores the growing financial muscle and institutional maturity of Indian-American philanthropy — a community estimated to donate $3–5 billion annually. For NRIs debating where to direct their giving, the evening offers a case study in how scale, accountability, and marquee honourees can move the needle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Minister Called Them a 'Butter Chicken Tsunami.' A Preacher Threatened to Burn Their Temples. Then New Zealand Rolled Out the Red Carpet.
articles.excerpt: As Modi and Luxon elevated ties to a strategic partnership and 10,000 cheered at Auckland's Spark Arena, New Zealand's 300,000 Indians confronted a parallel reality — one defined by 4,767 hate incidents, death threats, and a political appetite for anti-migrant rhetoric.
articles.image_caption: The Auckland skyline, where PM Modi addressed Indian New Zealanders at the Kia Ora Modi event at Spark Arena
articles.nri_angle: New Zealand's 292,000-strong Indian diaspora faces the sharpest disconnect in the democratic world: courted as strategic partners at the state level while enduring the highest rate of racially motivated abuse in the country. The story maps the lived experience of Indians navigating hate crimes, political slurs, and temple threats in a nation that simultaneously seeks their trade, their talent, and their tourism dollars.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twenty-Five Thousand Devotees, Three Chariots, Fifty Years: ISKCON's Golden Jubilee Is Rolling Across North America
articles.excerpt: From a Manhattan street where a young property developer once lent his land for the first parade to a continent-wide circuit drawing tens of thousands, the Hare Krishna chariot festival marks half a century in the West.
articles.image_caption: Devotees pull a decorated chariot during a Ratha Yatra festival in the United States
articles.nri_angle: The Ratha Yatra's 50-year arc mirrors the Indian diaspora's own journey in North America — from a handful of immigrants improvising a chariot parade in 1976 to a sprawling cultural institution that now anchors Hindu community life in dozens of cities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Forty-Nine Years of Prayers, Dosas, and New Beginnings: Inside America's Second-Oldest Hindu Temple on Its Birthday
articles.excerpt: On July 4th, as the United States marked 250 years, the Ganesh Temple in Flushing, Queens, celebrated its own anniversary — a quieter milestone that traces the entire arc of Hindu community-building in America.
articles.image_caption: The exterior of the Hindu Temple Society of North America in Flushing, Queens, New York
articles.nri_angle: The Flushing temple's story is the diaspora's story in miniature — a community of immigrants who arrived after the 1965 Immigration Act, pooled their resources, bought a former church, and built a spiritual anchor that has served generations. Its anniversary falling on July 4th is a coincidence that became a tradition, quietly linking the Indian-American journey to the American one.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seventy-One Per Cent Disapprove, Thirty-One Per Cent Have Gone Quiet on Social Media. Inside the Landmark Survey That Maps Indian America's Political Anxiety.
articles.excerpt: The Carnegie Endowment's 2026 Indian American Attitudes Survey of 1,000 adults reveals a community whose partisan loyalties are loosening, whose daily habits are shifting under the weight of discrimination — and whose frustration with American politics now outranks fear of racism as the reason some consider leaving.
articles.image_caption: A Diwali celebration in the United States — a landmark survey finds 71% of Indian Americans disapprove of the current political direction (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The survey maps exactly how the 5.2-million-strong Indian American community is processing political volatility, online hate, and shifting identity — and how those forces are changing what they wear, where they travel, and whether they speak up in public.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Overhauled the OCI Card System for Five Million Holders Worldwide. Here Is What Changed — and What You Need to Do.
articles.excerpt: The Ministry of Home Affairs has introduced fully digital OCI applications, an electronic OCI card option, a $25 fine for non-compliance, and expanded eligibility — the biggest update to the programme since 2013.
articles.image_caption: An Overseas Citizen of India card — India has now introduced a digital e-OCI alternative alongside the physical document
articles.nri_angle: Every OCI holder abroad — from the tech worker in San Jose to the retiree in London — is affected by these rule changes. The new compliance requirements, especially the passport-update window and $25 fine, demand immediate attention from the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anti-Sikh Hate Crimes Surged 3,700 Per Cent in a Decade. Anti-Hindu Incidents Hit a Record. The Numbers Keep Getting Worse.
articles.excerpt: FBI data for 2025 shows hate crimes against Sikhs, Hindus, and Buddhists reached their highest levels ever recorded, even as temples from California to Melbourne are being defaced with alarming regularity.
articles.image_caption: A Sikh gurdwara in the United States — anti-Sikh hate crimes have surged 3,700% over the last decade (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For Indian Americans — especially Sikhs and Hindus whose faith is visually identifiable — the surge in hate crimes is reshaping daily decisions: whether to wear a turban to the grocery store, whether to let children walk to the gurdwara alone, and whether America still feels like home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ten Thousand Telugu Americans Are Heading to Charlotte Next Week. An Oscar Winner Will Be Waiting.
articles.excerpt: The Telangana American Telugu Association's Mega Convention brings three days of concerts, CME sessions, dance battles, and diaspora soul-searching to the Carolina Convention Center — with a second blockbuster gathering in Baltimore right behind it.
articles.image_caption: The Charlotte Convention Center in North Carolina, venue for the TTA Mega Convention 2026
articles.nri_angle: Telugu Americans — among the fastest-growing sub-communities in the Indian diaspora — are building conventions that rival political party gatherings in scale, blending cultural preservation with professional networking and healthcare education.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Forty Per Cent More Indian Tech Workers Moved Home Last Year. Silicon Valley Is Starting to Notice.
articles.excerpt: LinkedIn data confirms a dramatic reverse-migration surge as H-1B costs spike, GCCs multiply, and a generation of senior engineers decides that Bangalore's upside now outweighs the Bay Area's.
articles.image_caption: The International Tech Park in Bangalore, one of India's largest technology hubs absorbing returning diaspora talent
articles.nri_angle: The reverse-migration wave is rewriting the traditional NRI career script — for the first time in decades, experienced Indian-origin professionals are choosing to leave the US not because of failure but because India's opportunities now compete with Silicon Valley's. The shift raises existential questions for the diaspora: is the dream of an American career still the default, or has the calculus permanently changed?
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Americans Gave Up to Five Billion Dollars Last Year. The Community's Philanthropy Gap Is Finally Closing.
articles.excerpt: A landmark survey shows Indian American giving has more than doubled as a share of income since 2018, shrinking a long-documented philanthropy deficit — and a new generation of donors is rewriting the playbook.
articles.image_caption: M.R. Rangaswami, founder of Indiaspora, which has helped drive Indian American giving to an estimated  billion annually (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For years, the Indian American community — despite being the highest-earning ethnic group in the US — was known for a stubborn philanthropy gap. This new data shows that gap is finally closing, driven by organised giving campaigns, generational shifts, and a growing sense that giving back is integral to diaspora identity. The trend matters to every NRI navigating the dual pull of contributing to both American and Indian causes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Uranium, Half a Billion Dollars, and a Wall of Indian Flags: What Actually Happened When Modi Landed in Melbourne
articles.excerpt: Australia struck a historic uranium export deal, its largest pension fund committed $347 million to India, and far-right protesters outside Marvel Stadium were outnumbered a thousand to one. For a million Indian Australians, the message was hard to miss.
articles.image_caption: Marvel Stadium in Melbourne's Docklands, venue for the 'Melbourne Meets Modi' diaspora event
articles.nri_angle: One million Indian Australians are the country's largest overseas-born population. The uranium deal and AustralianSuper investment validate the community's decades-long argument that India is a reliable destination for Australian capital — while the far-right protest outside Marvel Stadium underscores the backlash their visibility now attracts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Eaton's Factory Floors to a NASDAQ Corner Office: Pratik Trivedi Is CTS Corporation's New Chief Executive
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin executive took the helm of the $560-million sensor and components maker on July 6, extending the diaspora's quiet takeover of American industry's C-suite.
articles.image_caption: CTS Corporation trades on the New York Stock Exchange, where Pratik Trivedi now leads as Chief Executive Officer (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Trivedi's appointment extends the growing list of Indian-origin CEOs running American public companies — from P&G to Vanguard to Apple's COO — a pattern rooted in deep technical expertise and long operational tenures that the diaspora's career architecture uniquely produces.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Days, Zero Tickets Required: Lincoln Center's India Week Returns With Garba, Comedy, and the Biggest Silent Disco in South Asian New York
articles.excerpt: From a sunrise Rajasthani folk concert to an all-star comedy night featuring Aasif Mandvi, New York's most iconic performing arts campus hands its stages to the diaspora — and every event is free.
articles.image_caption: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts in New York City, the venue for India Week
articles.nri_angle: India Week is the largest curated celebration of Indian arts and culture at a major American performing arts institution, and every event is free — a deliberate message that Indian culture belongs on the country's biggest cultural stages, not behind a paywall.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nita Ambani Proposes an India-America Health Alliance at AAPI's Sold-Out Tampa Convention. The Diaspora's Physicians Are Listening.
articles.excerpt: The Reliance Foundation chairperson received the AAPI Humanitarian Award and the Key to the City of Tampa, then outlined a three-pillar partnership — access, capacity, discovery — that would yoke America's largest bloc of Indian-origin doctors to India's public health infrastructure.
articles.image_caption: Nita Ambani, Founder and Chairperson of Reliance Foundation
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin physicians are the single largest ethnic bloc in American medicine, and AAPI is their institutional voice. The proposed India-America Health Alliance would channel diaspora medical expertise back into India's healthcare system — turning professional success abroad into public health impact at home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thirty-Seven Charged, Twenty-Four Arrested: The US Crackdown on Indian Crime Gangs That Extorted the Diaspora
articles.excerpt: Operation Hard Ball has unsealed indictments against three India-based organised crime groups accused of assassinations, extortion of NRIs in California, and trafficking across two continents.
articles.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: The Bishnoi and Bhagwanpuria gangs directly targeted NRI community leaders and business figures in the US and Canada through extortion, using threats of violence delivered via WhatsApp. A Thousand Oaks, California resident was allegedly threatened with a $5 million demand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Jewels, One Community: Inside AIA–New York's 2026 Gala Honouring the Diaspora's Finest
articles.excerpt: From a Padma Bhushan oncologist to a Harvard MBA building an AI startup, the oldest Indian American organisation celebrated the professionals who define the community's ambition.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Dattatreyudu Nori receiving the Padma Shri from President Pranab Mukherjee at Rashtrapati Bhavan in 2015
articles.nri_angle: AIA-NY, founded in 1967 as the first national association of Asian Indians in America, honoured seven professionals across medicine, law, tech, and business — a snapshot of the Indian American community's evolution from a small immigrant group to a five-million-strong professional powerhouse.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At Twenty-Three, a Haryana-Born Councillor Becomes the Youngest Indian-Origin Mayor in Britain
articles.excerpt: Tushar Kumar, a King's College London graduate who was first elected at twenty, has been appointed mayor of Elstree and Borehamwood — the latest in a growing wave of young Indian-origin politicians winning civic office across Britain and America.
articles.image_caption: Indian-origin politicians are winning civic office across Britain at every level — Tushar Kumar, 23, just became the youngest Indian-origin mayor in the country (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Tushar Kumar, 23, from Haryana becomes the youngest Indian-origin mayor in Britain, part of a growing wave of young British-Indian and Indian-American politicians entering civic leadership across the UK and US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From OpenAI to Anthropic to Apple: Indian-Origin Engineers Now Run the AI Departments That Run the World
articles.excerpt: A quiet rearrangement of power at the top of Silicon Valley's most consequential companies has placed Indian-origin technologists in charge of building, shipping, and scaling artificial intelligence — the technology that every government and corporation on earth is now scrambling to master.
articles.image_caption: Google CEO Sundar Pichai, part of the generation of Indian-origin tech leaders who rose through Silicon Valley's engineering ranks — a pipeline that is now placing Indian-origin CTOs at OpenAI, Anthropic, and Apple
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers now hold CTO and VP-level AI roles at OpenAI, Anthropic, Apple, Meta, Tesla, and Microsoft — a structural shift that places the diaspora at the centre of the technology defining the next decade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Hundred and Fifty Thousand Indian New Zealanders Are About to Meet a Prime Minister Who Took Forty Years to Arrive
articles.excerpt: Modi's July 10 visit to New Zealand will be the first by an Indian PM in four decades. For a diaspora that now makes up six per cent of the country and generates $350 million in GDP, it is less a diplomatic event than a recognition long overdue.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi — his upcoming visit to New Zealand will be the first by an Indian PM in 40 years
articles.nri_angle: New Zealand's Indian community — now 350,000 strong and six per cent of the population — awaits the first visit by an Indian PM in 40 years, navigating between diplomatic warmth and tightening immigration rules.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Received a Record $145 Billion From Its Diaspora. For the First Time, America Sent the Most.
articles.excerpt: Inward remittances hit $144.79 billion in FY26, up from $124.55 billion the year before. The bigger story is where the money is coming from — and what the shift says about who the Indian diaspora has become.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai — India received a record 44.79 billion in diaspora remittances in FY26
articles.nri_angle: America is now the single largest source of remittances to India, overtaking the Gulf — a data-driven confirmation of the diaspora's shift from blue-collar Gulf workers to white-collar US professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
